title: Normalized lifting of sectionwise module actions to internal sheaf modules
statement:
Let $C$ be a site essentially small relative to the universe of abelian coefficient groups. Use abelian sheafification $a$ [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] and the sheafified objectwise tensor over $\mathbf Z$, for which $a$ is strong symmetric monoidal [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor]. Let $B$ be a sheaf of commutative rings, with its internal ring structure characterized by extension of pointwise multiplication and unit [det-def-sfb-ring-object-sheaf]. Let $P$ be an abelian sheaf, equipped on its underlying presheaf with a natural action $\beta:B\otimes_pP\to P$, where $\otimes_p$ is objectwise $\otimes_{\mathbf Z}$. Assume its sectionwise action is unital and associative: $\beta(e^p(n)\otimes x)=nx$ and $\beta(bc\otimes x)=\beta(b\otimes\beta(c\otimes x))$, with $e^p(n)=n\cdot1$. Write $\epsilon_P:aP\xrightarrow{\sim}P$ for the sheafification counit. Then
$$\gamma_P=\epsilon_P\circ a(\beta):B\otimes P=a(B\otimes_pP)\longrightarrow P$$
is the unique sheaf morphism extending $\beta$ along the canonical map from the tensor presheaf, and it satisfies the internal unit and associativity identities of [sk-def-sfb-module-objects]. For two such sheaves $P,Q$, an additive natural map $v:P\to Q$ is a morphism of their resulting internal $B$-modules if and only if $v\beta_P=\beta_Q(\mathrm{id}_B\otimes_pv)$. The assignment leaves underlying abelian sheaves and maps unchanged, respects identities, composition and sums, and so is an additive functor on the category of such sectionwise module sheaves (with the displayed action-commuting maps). For a finite family of such objects, the abelian sheaf $L(U)=\prod_iP_i(U)$ with coordinate restrictions and action $\beta_L(b\otimes(x_i)_i)=(\beta_{P_i}(b\otimes x_i))_i$ is again such an object; its lifted coordinate cone is a product of internal $B$-modules. Equivalently every family of internal module maps $v_i:K\to P_i$, with $K$ any internal $B$-module, has a unique internal-linear tuple map to this lifted $L$. For the empty family $L$ is the zero sheaf and is terminal. For $P=B$ and $\beta=\mu^p$, the lifted action is the given internal multiplication $\mu$, hence the resulting module is the regular internal $B$-module.

proof.text: Write $i$ for inclusion into abelian presheaves and $\eta_F:F\to iaF$ for the sheafification unit. The universal property in [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] says that precomposition with $\eta_F$ bijects sheaf maps $aF\to P$ with presheaf maps $F\to iP$. For a sheaf $P$, the extension $\epsilon_P:a(iP)\to P$ of its identity is inverse to $\eta_{iP}$: one composite is the identity by extension, and the other by uniqueness. Naturality of $\eta$ now gives $i(\epsilon_Pa\beta)\eta_{B\otimes_pP}=i\epsilon_P\eta_{iP}\beta=\beta$. Thus the displayed $\gamma_P$ exists and is the unique extension. In particular two sheaf maps out of $aF$ agree whenever their restrictions to $F$ agree.

proof.text: The unit and associative hypotheses define a module object over the coefficient presheaf: prove the unit equation on n tensor x and the associative equation on (b tensor c) tensor x, using additive generation by pure tensors. These are precisely the axioms of [sk-def-sfb-module-objects].

source.place: Unit and unitor bullets; apply the sheafification universal property to the sectionwise unit law

proof.text: Strong monoidal sheafification from [det-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor-structure] transports this presheaf module to a module over the sheafified coefficient. Transport both objects along the counit isomorphisms of [def-weil-pbc-sheafification], using ModObj.ofIso and Functor.modObjObj. The coefficient transport is definitionally the prescribed monoid of [det-def-sfb-ring-object-sheaf]. The transported action is the inverse counits tensor, the sheafification tensorator, the sheafified action, and the module counit. By the definition of the specified tensor comparison this is exactly gamma. Thus the transported unit and associative laws are the required laws of [sk-def-sfb-module-objects].

source.place: Associator bullet and its invertible sheafified unit comparisons; apply to the sectionwise associativity identity

proof.text: An additive natural map $v:P\to Q$ is already a map of abelian sheaves, since the sheaf category is full in presheaves. By the tensor-on-morphisms formula of [det-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor-structure] and naturality of the sheafification unit, the restrictions of $v\gamma_P$ and $\gamma_Q(\mathrm{id}_B\otimes v)$ to $B\otimes_pP$ are exactly $v\beta_P$ and $\beta_Q(\mathrm{id}_B\otimes_pv)$. The bijection of step 1 says that equality holds before restriction if and only if it holds afterwards. The former is precisely the module-morphism equation of [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], proving both directions of the criterion.

source.place: First two sentences: linearity of the coordinate isomorphism; normalized extension of the action-commuting equation

proof.text: The identity commutes with each $\beta$, and for action-commuting $v:P\to Q$ and $w:Q\to H$ one has $(wv)\beta_P=w\beta_Q(\mathrm{id}\otimes_pv)=\beta_H(\mathrm{id}\otimes_p(wv))$. Also $(v+w)\beta_P=\beta_Q(\mathrm{id}\otimes_p(v+w))$ by additivity of $\beta_Q$, and the zero map commutes with the actions. Step 4 therefore gives the functor on the specified objects and maps. Identities, composition, zero and sums are unchanged on underlying natural maps. The same bilinear calculation shows that sums of internal-linear maps are internal-linear (or apply step 4 to their underlying maps). Consequently this functor is additive.

source.place: First two sentences: passage from continuous linear coordinate maps to internal module maps; additive functor assertion

proof.text: Construct the presheaf with section groups Shrink(product_i P_i(U)), canonically additively equivalent to the full coordinate product. Finiteness makes this group small in the coefficient universe even when the index has an independent universe. Coordinate restrictions and tuple maps give a limiting presheaf Fan. Limits of sheaves are sheaves, by Sheaf.isSheaf_of_isLimit. Apply [lem-sfb-modobj-forget-creates] in the presheaf category to obtain the module action; its projection equations evaluated at b tensor x give exactly the coordinate action formula. Lift this object and its linear projections by the preceding steps.

source.place: Coordinate isomorphism to a finite power: coordinatewise action, gluing and product cone

proof.text: Apply limit reflection for Mod.forget from [lem-sfb-modobj-forget-creates] to the lifted coordinate cone and its underlying abelian sheaf product cone. This proves the universal property against every internal source module. For an empty index, isLimitEquivIsTerminalOfIsEmpty makes both cones terminal; IsTerminal.isZero makes the underlying abelian sheaf zero.

source.place: Finite power in the first two sentences: internal-module universal property, including arbitrary source and empty family

proof.text: For $P=B$ with $\beta=\mu^p$, the given multiplication $\mu$ is the unique sheaf morphism extending $\mu^p$ by [det-def-sfb-ring-object-sheaf]. Step 1 characterizes $\gamma_B$ by exactly that extension property. Thus $\gamma_B=\mu$, and the definition of the regular module in [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] identifies the output with the given regular internal module, on the same underlying sheaf.

source.place: Multiplication is the unique extension of the objectwise ring multiplication
